title: Selection-for-prediction: rethinking early cognitive development
title_zh: 基于选择的预测：重新思考早期认知发展
abstract: For decades, core knowledge accounts have proposed that early cognition is organized by innate, domain-specific conceptual or concept-like representations of objects, physical events, number, and agents. I propose a different starting point: infants' behaviors may arise from domain-general attentional priors-evolutionarily shaped selection biases-interacting with perceptual mechanisms that organize information and support perceptual prediction, rather than from abstract, postperceptual representations. Attentional priors favor ecologically consequential information, including continuity, contact, and synchrony. When such information is disrupted, perceptual prediction error-rather than conceptual contradiction-may produce violation-of-expectation effects. Grounded in constraints on visual input and neural processing, this framework accounts for early successes and systematic failures, suggesting that development begins with perceptual-attentional mechanisms that shape selection, organization, prediction, and learning.
abstract_zh: 几十年来，核心知识理论认为早期认知由先天的、领域特定的概念或类似概念的对象、物理事件、数量和代理人表示所组织。我提出一个不同的起点：婴儿的行为可能源于领域通用的注意先验——进化塑造的选择偏差——与组织信息并支持感知预测的感知机制相互作用，而非抽象的后感知表示。注意先验偏好生态上重要的信息，包括连续性、接触和同步性。当这些信息被破坏时，感知预测误差——而非概念矛盾——可能产生违期望效应。基于对视觉输入和神经处理的约束，这一框架解释了早期成功与系统性失败，表明发展始于塑造选择、组织、预测和学习的感知-注意机制。
